subject: ventures/youtube-chapters-check
professional: a YouTube channel manager / video SEO specialist who also exports markers from Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve; first checks: the three published chapter rules at their exact boundaries, the last chapter against the video length, SMPTE frame-rate conversion at 23.976/29.97, Resolve marker EDLs read by marker name, and a cleaned list that never loses a chapter silently

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with node scratchpad/yt/probe.mjs against sources the author did not write. SMPTE ST 12-1 non-drop: 01:00:00:00 at 29.97 = 108000 x 1001/30000 = 3603.6 s, tool 3603.6 (was 3600); 00:30:00:00 at 23.976 = 43200 x 1001/24000 = 1801.8 s, tool 1801.8 (was 1800). Drop-frame: 00:01:00;02 at 29.97 is frame 1800 = 60.06 s, tool 60.067 (labels treated as wall time, within 0.01 s); 00:10:00;00 = 17982 frames = 599.9994 s, tool 600. Resolve marker EDL (CMX3600, 01:00:00:00 start, |M: names) at 24 and 29.97 fps -> '0:00 Intro / 2:30 Setup / 10:00 Wrap up', no errors (at 29.97, 01:02:30:00 - start = 4500 frames x 1001/30000 = 150.15 s, floored 2:30, right). YouTube boundaries unchanged and right: 0:00/0:10/0:20 clean, 0:09 flagged, 0:01 start flagged, 1:60 'Not a valid time', last chapter 2:55 flagged at length 3:04, clean at 3:05. WebVTT 'A --> B' now written 'A -> B'. Still wrong (low): '0:00 - 1:30 Intro' gives title '1:30 Intro'; Audacity labels with a decimal comma give 'No timestamps found'. The YouTube help page (answer 9884579) could not be re-fetched this session (proxy 403 for support.google.com); the rules are taken from the 2026-11-17 audit's live fetch.
evidence.completeness: Every 2026-11-17 failure re-run. DaVinci Resolve 'Timeline Markers to EDL' conversion now works end to end on an EDL in Resolve's layout (including a '* comment' line, drop-frame FCM, unnamed marker -> blank-title error, 00:00:00:00 start not shifted; calc.test.mjs:151-189); README Known gaps says the fixtures are hand-written, not a file exported from Resolve. The cleaned list now names every line it leaves out ('Left out line 6 ("11:75 The part everyone gets wrong"): its time is impossible'). Premiere, Audacity '.' decimals, offset, intro, reorder, repeats and the four exports still pass. Open: range lines, comma-decimal Audacity, no note when the last chapter cannot be checked, an unparseable length silently ignored on the page (index.html options()).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/youtube-chapters-check && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 40 tests, 40 pass, 131 ms (30 at the last audit). Twelve seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: all five from 2026-11-17 now caught (<= 10, MIN_CHAPTERS 2, frame divisor, 59 ceiling, first-chapter > 1), plus SMPTE rate formula, drop-frame branch, EDL start-hour removal, EDL |M: names, WebVTT '-->' sanitising, repair's left-out note: all caught. One survived: 'Starts after the video ends' `>=` -> `>` (no test of a chapter exactly at the length). 11 of 12 caught.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (292 lines), the index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, repair-fuzz.test.mjs. The new EDL parser and SMPTE branch are small, commented with the standard they follow, and pure; the fuzz test checks repair is idempotent over seeded mutations. Defects: an unparseable video length is dropped without a word on the page (options() returns null); the 4-part regex fallback in parseTimestamp duplicates the main one; EDL detection is all-or-nothing on line shapes (one stray line falls back to the line parser, which then reads event lines as garbage).
evidence.claims: Backed now: 'convert ... DaVinci ... marker exports' (README.md:6, index.html:59, FAQ :118) by calc.test.mjs EDL tests and the probe, with the hand-written-fixture limit disclosed in README Known gaps; 'set the frame rate to match your sequence' now converts 23.976/29.97 right. Still off: the fix note 'Anything that cannot be proven is left as it was and named above' (index.html:184) sits above a change list that says an impossible-time line was left out, so the two sentences contradict (the drop itself is disclosed, so low); the 'Why won't my chapters show up?' FAQ still omits the channel-level causes the help page names (strikes, possibly inappropriate content). Disclaimer, non-affiliation and no-network test unchanged and present.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through again: a hand-typed description list is checked and cleaned in a minute; a Premiere editor at 29.97 or 23.976 now gets chapters on the right second at the end of a 3-hour stream (10.8 s early before); a Resolve user can paste a marker EDL and get named chapters from 0:00. Remaining first-hour gaps are small: a creator who writes ranges gets the end time in every title, a European Audacity user gets nothing, and a creator whose chapters fail for a strike is told the list is fine with no hint why.
evidence.domain: Against YouTube's published rules the checks are exact at every boundary. SMPTE ST 12-1 non-drop at 1000/1001 rates now counts nominal frames per labelled second; drop-frame labels are treated as wall time, which is the standard's intent and within a frame. Resolve EDLs: CMX3600 record-in, |M: marker-name comments, FCM drop flag, timeline start removed on the label before conversion (right, since NDF is linear in frames). W3C WebVTT cue payload rule now respected. Formats cited from my own knowledge except the YouTube page (via the previous audit's fetch).

verdict: Meets the bar now. PRs #17049 and #17156 closed all five of the 2026-11-17 defects they were recorded against, and the re-check confirms it by running, not reading: SMPTE non-drop recomputes exactly (3603.6 s and 1801.8 s), a Resolve marker EDL becomes named chapters from 0:00 at 24 and 29.97 fps, the cleaned list names the line it leaves out, WebVTT titles are sanitised, and 11 of 12 seeded mutants fail a test (1 of 5 last time). The three low prior defects no fix PR claimed are still open (range-line titles and comma-decimal Audacity labels; the missing strikes cause; the silent no-length case), plus a contradictory fix-note sentence and one untested boundary. All six are low. Scores are for the code before this round's fix PR.
